title: Douro Field Blends: Quintas, Tawnies & the Pocinho Line
subRegion: Alto Douro Vinhateiro, Baixo Corgo, Cima Corgo & Douro Superior

bestPeriod.avoid: July-early August, Douro Superior regularly exceeds 40°C in schist canyons with no shade; also January-February, when many quintas close entirely

accommodation.note: Quinta guesthouse €100, €170 pppn; two nights in Gaia/Porto €90, €140

food.note: Quinta lunch €25, €40; Régua tasca mains €10, €16; one starred dinner €90, €150

transport.note: Car 5 days, Linha do Douro tickets, one rabelo leg, driver day

activities.note: 9-11 tastings €12, €45, port lodge tours €20, €35, olive mill, treading session

profile.difficultyNote: 2/5, steep terrace walking on loose schist, long cellar stairs, one optional treading session

gatewayAirport: OPO Porto Francisco Sá Carneiro, 1 h 45 min drive to Peso da Régua, 2 h 10 min to Pinhão
summary: The Douro is a landscape argument: pre-phylloxera field blends of forty varieties planted together on schist terraces so steep the region needed UNESCO protection to justify farming them at all. The week runs upriver from the softer, wetter Baixo Corgo through the Cima Corgo heartland at Pinhão to the near-desert Douro Superior, learning the port hierarchy, ruby, LBV, tawny, colheita, vintage, before circling back to Vila Nova de Gaia to see where those casks actually age. Dry Douro DOC reds are now half the story and get equal time. Trains, a rabelo leg and a driver day mean nobody has to stay sober on the switchbacks.

itinerary.title: Porto, Gaia lodges, and the shape of port
itinerary.morning: Land at OPO, drop bags in Porto and walk the Ribeira down to the Dom Luís I bridge.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to **Vila Nova de Gaia** for **Taylor's** (scale, the 20-year tawny) and **Graham's 1890 Lodge** (museum, a vintage flight). The point is the cool damp lodge air that makes tawny possible and the Douro heat impossible.
itinerary.evening: **Taberna dos Mercadores** in the Ribeira, or **The Yeatman**'s cellar list if you want the full vertical.
itinerary.dayStats: 2 lodges / tours €20, €35 each / 20-year tawny bottle €40, €60, 40-year €120, €180 / no driving today
itinerary.sleep: Hotel in Porto Ribeira or Gaia

itinerary.title: The Linha do Douro to Régua and the Baixo Corgo
itinerary.morning: Train from Porto Campanhã to **Peso da Régua**, roughly 2 h, sitting on the right after Mosteirô for the first river views.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Museu do Douro** for demarcation history, then **Quinta do Vallado** outside town, Baixo Corgo fruit, a schist-clad modern winery, and a side-by-side of Douro DOC red against port.
itinerary.evening: **Castas e Pratos** in the converted railway warehouse; order posta and the house Douro red.
itinerary.dayStats: Train €13, €18, 2 h / 1 quinta / Vallado tasting €15, €30 / museum €7.50 / Douro DOC red €12, €30
itinerary.sleep: Quinta do Vallado or Hotel Régua Douro, Peso da Régua

itinerary.title: Pinhão, Bomfim and the Cima Corgo
itinerary.morning: Régua-Pinhão by train (25 min) for the station's azulejo panels, then **Quinta do Bomfim**, terrace tasting above the line, Dow's and Warre's, and the walk through the vineyard blocks.
itinerary.afternoon: A rabelo hour on the river from Pinhão quay, then **Quinta de la Rosa** for a second, smaller-scale visit and its riverside terrace.
itinerary.evening: **Restaurante DOC** at Folgosa, on a deck built over the water, for Rui Paula's tasting menu, or the far cheaper **Veladouro** in Pinhão.
itinerary.dayStats: Train 25 min, €3, €5 / 2 quintas / Bomfim €20, €45 / rabelo €15, €25, 1 h / DOC menu €90, €150
itinerary.sleep: Quinta de la Rosa or Vintage House Hotel, Pinhão

itinerary.title: Field blends, Crasto and treading if the season allows
itinerary.morning: Driver day. **Quinta do Crasto** above Gouvinhas for the Vinha Maria Teresa old-vine field blend and the infinity pool that appears in every photograph of the region.
itinerary.afternoon: **Quinta Nova de Nossa Senhora do Carmo** at Covas do Douro, vineyard trail, wine museum, and the best quinta lunch on the river.
itinerary.evening: In late September, a **lagar treading session** where one is offered, barefoot in granite tanks, two hours of cutting and liberdade, and a real understanding of why port is fortified mid-ferment.
itinerary.dayStats: 48 km driving, all switchbacks / 2 quintas / fees €25, €45 / driver day €300, €450 per car / treading session €30, €60 where offered
itinerary.sleep: Quinta de la Rosa or Vintage House Hotel, Pinhão

itinerary.title: Favaios moscatel, bread and olive oil
itinerary.morning: Climb 400 m out of the valley to **Favaios** on the plateau. The **Adega Cooperativa de Favaios** pours Moscatel do Douro, a style unrelated to port and made from Moscatel Galego Branco.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Museu do Pão e do Vinho** and the bakery for *pão de Favaios*, then down to **Quinta do Salgueiral** for a Douro DOP olive-oil tasting and a mill walk.
itinerary.evening: **O Lagar** in Régua for posta mirandesa cooked rare on a hot stone, and bola de carne from the morning's bakery for tomorrow's train.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1 co-op + 1 mill / Moscatel tasting €8, €15 / oil tasting €10, €18 / posta €18, €26 / Moscatel bottle €7, €14
itinerary.sleep: Quinta de la Rosa or Vintage House Hotel, Pinhão

itinerary.title: Douro Superior: Vale Meão and the Côa
itinerary.morning: Train east from Pinhão toward **Pocinho**, the end of the line, roughly 1 h 10 m through the tightest gorges of the route.
itinerary.afternoon: **Quinta do Vale Meão** at Foz Côa, the estate that once made Barca Velha, now the benchmark for Douro Superior concentration. Pair it with the **Côa Valley** Palaeolithic rock-art park if you hold a slot.
itinerary.evening: Back west, or overnight locally at **Quinta do Vallado Douro Superior**. Eat simply: grilled cabrito and a bottle of the estate's own red.
itinerary.dayStats: Train 1 h 10 m each way, €6, €10 / 1 quinta / Vale Meão tasting €25, €45 / Côa park visit €18 / Douro Superior red €25, €60
itinerary.sleep: Quinta do Vallado Douro Superior or back at Pinhão

itinerary.title: Tawny logic, and out via Gaia
itinerary.morning: Drive or train back west along the N222 Régua-Pinhão stretch, routinely called one of the world's best drives, stopping at the **Miradouro de São Leonardo de Galafura** at 640 m.
itinerary.afternoon: A last Gaia lodge, **Kopke** for colheitas, since it holds the deepest run of single-vintage tawnies and pours them by the glass by decade.
itinerary.evening: **Cantinho do Avillez** or **Casa Guedes** for a pernil sandwich before OPO.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km Pinhão-Gaia, 2 h / 1 lodge / Kopke colheita flight €20, €45 / colheita bottle €35, €90 / OPO 25 min from Gaia
itinerary.sleep: Airport hotel, or fly out same evening

accommodationStrategy.name: Quinta de la Rosa
accommodationStrategy.description: On the river below Pinhão with its own winery, restaurant and pool, so the Day 3 tasting is a walk downstairs and you never drive after dinner. €140, €230 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Quinta do Vallado
accommodationStrategy.description: Schist-and-slate modern building attached to a historic Baixo Corgo estate, five minutes from Régua station, which makes the train days frictionless. Its Douro Superior sister property at Vila Nova de Foz Côa lets you split the week without backtracking. €160, €260.

accommodationStrategy.name: Vintage House Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The reliable non-quinta option, a converted eighteenth-century estate building on the quay next to the rabelo moorings and 400 m from the station. Large rooms, river-facing terrace, €150, €240.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming applies. 4G is good in Régua and Pinhão, unreliable in the gorges east of Tua and on the Favaios plateau road. Download offline maps; quinta driveways are unnumbered.
logistics.emergency: 112. The main hospital is Centro Hospitalar de Vila Real, 40 min from Régua. Terrace falls on loose schist are the commonest injury, wear grip, not deck shoes.
logistics.weather: The valley is a heat trap, Pinhão runs up to 12°C warmer than Porto on the same afternoon, and the Douro Superior tops 40°C in July. Autumn river fog blanks the N222 viewpoints before 10:00.
logistics.bookingWindows: Quintas 2-4 weeks, longer for September; Crasto and Vale Meão 4-8 weeks. DOC Folgosa 3-6 weeks. Treading sessions sell out by August. Côa Valley rock-art slots are capped and released online ahead.
logistics.money: Eurozone. Cards accepted at quintas and restaurants; village bakeries and the Favaios co-op shop are easier with cash. Tipping is 5-10% or rounding up.
logistics.transportRules: Blood-alcohol limit 0.5 g/l, and 0.2 g/l for licences under three years. The N222 and N323 are narrow, blind and unforgiving, do not drive them after tasting. Motorway tolls on the A4 use electronic gantries; take the rental company's transponder. CP changed Linha do Douro timetables and some Porto services now require a change at Caíde or Régua, verify on cp.pt before relying on a connection.
logistics.permits: Tasting fees of €12, €45 are standard and often credited against a purchase. The Alto Douro Vinhateiro is a UNESCO cultural landscape: no drones over quintas without permission, and terraces are private property.
logistics.health: Tap water is drinkable. Port is 19-20% abv, a five-glass flight is close to a bottle of table wine. Sun exposure on unshaded schist terraces is severe from May; carry water on any vineyard walk.

proTips: Sit on the right-hand side leaving Porto and the left returning. East of Mosteirô the Linha do Douro runs at water level and the wrong seat costs you the best forty minutes of the trip.
Taste an LBV and a 10-year tawny side by side at the same house. Same base wine, two ageing philosophies, it explains the whole port hierarchy faster than any tour.
Ask any quinta to show you a *vinha velha* block. The interplanted forty-variety field blends are being replanted to single varieties, and the old parcels are finite.
Buy port at the quinta, not in Gaia. The same bottle is routinely 20-30% cheaper upriver, and colheitas from small houses never reach the lodges' shops.
Book the Côa Valley rock-art park at the same time as your Douro Superior quinta. Both are near Vila Nova de Foz Côa, both are capped, and doing them separately wastes a two-hour drive.
Treading in a lagar is real work, not a photo op, two hours of chest-deep marching in cold must. Wear nothing you value and eat first.
The last ten days of October give harvest-free owners, full autumn colour and no 40°C afternoons. It is the single best week of the year here.

raw.The two DOCs: **DOC Porto** (fortified) and **DOC Douro** (unfortified) share one demarcated zone, the world's oldest at 1756. Three sub-regions: **Baixo Corgo** in the west, wettest and coolest, historically ruby and volume; **Cima Corgo** around Pinhão and Tua, the vintage-port heartland; **Douro Superior**, east to the Spanish border, hottest and least planted, now the source of the most concentrated dry reds.
raw.Grapes and field blends: The modern five are **Touriga Nacional**, **Touriga Franca**, **Tinta Roriz** (Tempranillo), **Tinta Barroca** and **Tinto Cão**. Old vineyards are **vinha velha** field blends, up to forty varieties interplanted and co-fermented, never separately identified.
raw.Port styles: **Ruby** and **LBV** (Late Bottled Vintage, from one year, bottled 4-6 years after harvest; unfiltered versions need decanting) age in bulk. **Tawny** with an indication of age, 10, 20, 30, 40 years, is a blend whose stated age is an average, aged oxidatively in small casks in Gaia's cool lodges. **Colheita** is a single-vintage tawny, minimum seven years in wood, with the year on the label. **Vintage** is declared only in outstanding years, roughly three times a decade, bottled after two years and aged in glass; each house declares independently, subject to IVDP approval. **Moscatel do Douro** from Favaios is a separate sweet speciality.
raw.Quintas open to visitors: **Quinta do Bomfim** (Symington, Pinhão) is the best-organised visit on the river, terrace tasting above the railway line, tours bookable online at roughly €20, €45 by flight, English standard, several daily. **Quinta Nova de Nossa Senhora do Carmo** (Covas do Douro) has a wine hotel, restaurant and vineyard trail. **Quinta do Crasto** (Gouvinhas) is known for the infinity pool and the Vinha Maria Teresa old-vine field blend; email well ahead. **Quinta do Vallado** (Régua) and **Quinta do Vale Meão** (Foz Côa) best show the west-east contrast; **Quinta de la Rosa** at Pinhão has rooms and a riverside restaurant. All need reservations, most answer email within days and prefer 2-4 weeks' notice, longer in September.
raw.Producers beyond wine: In **Favaios**, the **Adega Cooperativa de Favaios** for Moscatel and the **Museu do Pão e do Vinho**, where the four-cornered *pão de Favaios* is still baked. **Quinta do Salgueiral** near Régua for Douro DOP olive oil and mill visits. The essential dishes are **posta mirandesa**, a thick PDO Mirandesa steak served rare, canonically at **Restaurante O Lagar** in Régua, and **bola de carne**, the layered meat bread in every Régua bakery. **Restaurante DOC** at Folgosa (Rui Paula) is the river's benchmark kitchen; **Castas e Pratos** in Régua fills an old railway warehouse.
raw.Season and timing: Harvest runs roughly 25 August-end September, earliest in the Douro Superior. Foot treading in *lagares* runs through September and a few quintas let visitors join, usually in the evening, but that fortnight is also when owners have no time for you. Olive pressing follows in November; vine colour peaks in the last ten days of October.
raw.Transport and the sober-driving plan: Portugal's limit is 0.5 g/l, and 0.2 g/l for licences under three years. The **Linha do Douro** is the answer: Porto Campanhã-Régua roughly 2 h, Régua-Pinhão 25 min, Pinhão-Pocinho about 1 h 10 m, €5, €15, running at water level east of Régua. CP has restructured Douro schedules and some services now require a connection, check cp.pt the week before. Add a **rabelo** leg from Pinhão quay (€15, €25 an hour) and one driver day with **Douro Exclusive** or **Living Tours** at €300, €450 per car.

sources.verified: Symington's own visitor page for Quinta do Bomfim confirming it as a bookable visit-and-tasting site at Pinhão; CP's published alert that Linha do Douro schedules changed and services were restructured; the three-sub-region structure of the demarcated Douro and the separate legal existence of DOC Porto and DOC Douro; vintage-declaration practice, in which each house declares individually subject to IVDP approval.
sources.confidenceNotes: Tasting fees are estimated bands; Bomfim, Crasto, Vale Meão and Quinta Nova each price several tiers and change them seasonally. Linha do Douro journey times and through-service availability are the most volatile item here, confirm on cp.pt close to travel. Visitor treading sessions are offered by only some quintas in some vintages; do not promise one. Restaurante DOC and Castas e Pratos have seasonal closures. Rabelo quay prices are informal. Hotel rates are prior-season estimates.
